newsitem.title: CHINA: Strong aftershock jolts west China, some damage.
newsitem.headline: Strong aftershock jolts west China, some damage.

text.p: A strong after-shock measuring 5.2 on the Richter scale jolted China's northwestern Xinjiang region on Wednesday, causing more damage in an area where up to 50 people were killed in an earthquake last week.
The number of dead and injured from Wednesday's after-shock had yet to be determined, the official Xinhua news agency said.
The tremor rocked the Jiashi district at 4.20 p.m. (0620 GMT) on Wednesday, flattening houses and sheds and killing livestock, Xinhua said.

It was the 19th aftershock measuring more than 4.0 on the Richter scale to rock Jiashi since an earthquake of 6.4 magnitude caused widespread damage and killed up to 50 people on January 21, Xinhua said.
About 700 aftershocks have rocked the district, populated mainly by sheep herders and cotton farmers, toppling more than 400 mud-brick houses in the last eight days, it said.
Several dozen people were injured in last week's earthquake, that left thousands homeless and destroyed 14,000 houses.
Seismological officials had warned that an earthquake of up to 5.5 magnitude could strike the same area.
An earthquake of 6.9 magnitude rocked Jiashi last March, killing 26 people and injuring 128.
